_what: qal/widebank PHASE 1 -- THE BANK-WIDTH SWEEP. Pre-registered BEFORE the first deck of this directory. Question: per-gate QAL energy is predicted to fall with bank population N while level time rises as sqrt(N). Is there an N where per-gate energy beats CMOS inside a usable level time? Written by the agent that will run it; nothing in this file may be edited after the first deck -- corrections go to AMENDMENT.md with their own mtimes.

_order_of_work_witness.DISK_STATE_BEFORE.txt: written first; carries the sha256 of every committed input and the df, and the ls of this directory showing it as the only file
_order_of_work_witness.PRE_REGISTERED.json: this file; sha256 recorded in PRE_REGISTERED.sha256 immediately after writing
_order_of_work_witness.first_deck: btk/c_m10_T200_H4_dv1200_free.cir (the INSTRUMENT CHECK re-run), written only after both files above exist

CONFIGURATION -- only what is known to w.architecture: qal/banktank PER-BANK TANKS (commit 0aae11e) -- the only arrangement measured to compute unbuffered (32/32 gates value-correct at a 200 ps beat). Each bank raises its OWN rail from its OWN local tank C_tank = m*C_bank through its OWN inductor, and returns the charge to that same tank.
CONFIGURATION -- only what is known to w.dV_justification: MANDATED by the brief and by the block: below Vtn + |Vtp| = 0.9642 V the cascade is not level-restoring, and the 161-cell block fails 59/161 at dV=1.2. The committed banktank digit-check row is dV=1.2 because that is what is on disk; the SWEEP is dV=1.65.
CONFIGURATION -- only what is known to w.cell: sg13g2-class inverter, pMOS w=1.12u l=0.13u with supply AND bulk on the bank rail, nMOS w=0.74u l=0.13u, CL = 2.0 fF per output. VERBATIM from the committed harness. NOT swept here -- cell sizing is Phase 2.
CONFIGURATION -- only what is known to w.switch: committed tg15p triple: widths(total) = {wn: total/3, wp: 2*total/3, park: total/15}; park referenced to THIS BANK'S TANK (banktank amendment A6), anti-phase to the transfer gate. VGH = 1.5 V, EDGE = 2.0 ps.
CONFIGURATION -- only what is known to w.source_side_cut: STRUCTURALLY PRESENT AND UNCONDITIONAL in this architecture, which is why it is not an added device: bank k's tank island {C_tank(k), L(k), switch(k)} touches exactly ONE rail, so there is no idle downstream inductor for charge to divert into. chain3's finding-(d) source-side cut existed to stop 42.3% of hop charge diverting into the NEXT bank's idle inductor in a peer-fed chain; with per-bank tanks that path does not exist. The brief's 'source-side cuts on every hop' is therefore SATISFIED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by omission. I will verify it by measurement: A7 below gates |I(L_j)| of every NON-hopping inductor at the hopping bank's ZCS.
CONFIGURATION -- only what is known to w.buck: NOT simulated in this phase. The `free` mode (tank runs down, no recharge) is the measured primary, exactly as the committed working row. The converter that would resupply the measured tank loss is booked as a stated efficiency and its row is a BOUND, never a measurement. Rationale stated here so it cannot be claimed later as a measurement: adding the fixed buck at 6 N points x 3 T points is not affordable inside this phase's runtime budget, and the buck multiplies the tank-loss term by 1/eta without changing its N-scaling, which is the quantity under test.
CONFIGURATION -- only what is known to w.probe_protocol: committed TRUE-ZCS probe-then-cut, sequential: for each phase (rise, return) and each bank k in order, banks < k are cut at their own measured zeros, bank k closes and never opens, and t_zcs is the first interpolated sign change of I(L_k) after its peak. banktank amendment A7 is carried: zeros are probed at the row's OWN T and H, not at a reference schedule.
CONFIGURATION -- only what is known to w.metering: 1F integrators only (CX=1F, BX current source, RX=0.01). Every integrator t0-referenced by subtracting its own value at the Z checkpoint (t=0.5 ps). Tank loss additionally cross-checked convention-free as 0.5*C_tank*(V0^2 - V1^2) because C_tank is a LINEAR capacitor.
CONFIGURATION -- only what is known to w.models: PSP103 via .hdl + sg13g2_psp103_tt.lib, sg13_lv via qal/sg13lv_compat.sp. JUNCAP200 enabled by model defaults; the shim's default PD = 1.00 um is smaller than the 1.12 um pMOS so the STI-edge term clips to zero -- leakage numbers are LOWER BOUNDS and must be labelled so. tt corner only; no vt/gmin hacks; unique .va module names not needed (single .hdl).
CONFIGURATION -- only what is known to w.cache: PRIVATE PYMS_VAE_CACHE = /tmp/claude-1001/-usr-local-src/4921ad0c-f17b-4b84-986a-5917c9ebd2a6/scratchpad/vae_cache_widebank. Warmed SEQUENTIALLY by a single tiny deck before any concurrent launch (the committed race trap).

DECK STRUCTURE.why_3_not_4: bank 1 = chain head (8..256 ideal DC input sources), bank 2 = THE BANK UNDER TEST (its inputs ARE bank 1's output nodes and its outputs ARE bank 3's gate nets -- a real predecessor and a real receiver, both at chain-delivered rails), bank 3 = the real receiver whose own delivered rail the functional criterion needs. Every number reported for a sweep point is bank 2's. Dropping bank 4 is a 25% device saving that the per-bank-tank architecture makes free, because nothing but bank k touches tank k. VALIDATED, not asserted: at N=8 the NBANK=3 deck's bank-2 row is compared digit-by-digit against the NBANK=4 committed-configuration deck's bank 2 (acceptance A0b).
DECK STRUCTURE.gates_are_identical: one bank = N identical inverters, as the brief specifies.
DECK STRUCTURE.pattern: PAT = [1,1,1,0,1,0,0,1] TILED N/8 times. Holds the HIGH fraction EXACTLY 5/8 at every N, so the activity fraction is a controlled constant across the sweep and the only thing that changes is population. DECLARED CONSEQUENCE (not a discovery): a tiled pattern on identical cells with identical 2 fF loads makes every gate in a bank a member of one of exactly TWO electrical classes, so 'per gate' yields two distinct trajectories per bank and CANNOT catch a single-gate outlier. This is the committed record's own fixture caveat and it is inherited knowingly. It is mitigated two ways: (i) the VALUE and functional checks are evaluated on ALL N output nodes individually by .measure, so intra-class identity is MEASURED at the checkpoint rather than assumed, and (ii) one RANDOM-pattern control deck at the best N with the same HIGH count.
DECK STRUCTURE.printing_and_disk: df shows 8.0 G free. Per-gate .print columns at N=256 x 3 banks would be ~800 columns and hundreds of MB per deck. Therefore: .print carries rails, tanks, I(L), sw nodes and TWO representative output nodes per bank (one per electrical class); ALL N outputs of every bank are sampled by .measure FIND at the checkpoints. Probe .prn files are deleted after their zero is extracted. This is a disk decision, not a scientific one, and the thing it costs is stated: a continuous waveform exists only for the two class representatives, so any per-gate quantity that needs a trajectory (first-valid instant) is computed on the representatives and is valid only to the extent intra-class identity holds AT THE CHECKPOINTS, which is measured.
DECK STRUCTURE.timestep: pstep 0.1 ps, max step 0.25 ps at N=8 as committed. Because t_hop grows as sqrt(N), holding 0.25 ps at N=256 over a ~4x longer run is pure cost; max step is scaled as 0.25*sqrt(N/8) ps. FALSIFICATION REQUIRED (A8): at N=64 the row is re-run at the unscaled 0.25 ps max step and the two must agree to the stated tolerance, or the scaled step is abandoned.

SCALING LAWS -- PRE-STATED, so the measu.C_bank(N): DERIVED 35.979 * N/8 fF (the committed MEASURED secant C of one 8-cell bank, scaled by population). MEASURED CHECK at every N: Q_through_L over the rise divided by the delivered rail swing must reproduce it to within 10%, or the scaling is wrong and the sweep axis is mislabelled.
SCALING LAWS -- PRE-STATED, so the measu.C_tank(N): m * C_bank(N) = 10 * 35.979 * N/8 fF. Tank pre-charge V_t0 = dV*(m+1)/(2m) = 0.9075 V at dV=1.65, unchanged with N (the lossless linear-LC value; it is a ratio, not an absolute).
SCALING LAWS -- PRE-STATED, so the measu.t_hop(N): PREDICTED to grow as sqrt(N) at fixed L: t_hop = pi*sqrt(L*C_eff), C_eff = C_bank*m/(m+1). Predicted t_zcs(N=256) = t_zcs(N=8)*sqrt(32) = 126.5*5.657 = 715.6 ps.
SCALING LAWS -- PRE-STATED, so the measu.I_pk(N): PREDICTED to grow as sqrt(N): V_t0*sqrt(C_eff/L). Predicted I_pk(256) = 1185 uA * 5.657 = 6.70 mA.
SCALING LAWS -- PRE-STATED, so the measu.W_switch(N) PRIMARY: 30 * sqrt(N/8) um nominal total width. REASON, pre-stated: the hop quality is set by the loop Q = (1/R_tot)*sqrt(L/C). sqrt(L/C) falls as 1/sqrt(N) at fixed L, so holding Q constant -- equivalently holding the fractional resonant loss pi/Q constant -- requires R_on, and hence 1/W, to fall as 1/sqrt(N). The SAME exponent follows independently from the drain requirement (I_pk*R_on <= a fixed fraction of dV). Values: 30 / 42.4 / 60 / 84.9 / 120 / 169.7 um.
SCALING LAWS -- PRE-STATED, so the measu.W_switch FALSIFICATION CONTROLS: at N=32 and N=256 the row is repeated at W/2 and 2W. The pre-stated signature of a CORRECT sqrt law is: W/2 degrades the delivered rail and the worst-gate margin measurably while 2W buys < 1% of delivered rail for ~2x the gate charge. If W/2 costs nothing, the sqrt law over-sizes the switch and the amortisation is BETTER than I predicted; if 2W is still gaining, it under-sizes it and the amortisation is WORSE.
SCALING LAWS -- PRE-STATED, so the measu.gate_charge: Q_gate = 0.155 fC per um of nominal total width, the committed qal/lsweep MEASURED linear fit (1.97/4.05/8.68/18.46/38.98 fC at 15/30/60/120/240 um). Its ideal-PWL drive energy on the same fit: 4.08/7.29/14.63/29.09/58.45 fJ. Both are carried as the DERIVED switch-drive term and BOTH are cross-checked against this study's own egt and ehi integrators at every N.
SCALING LAWS -- PRE-STATED, so the measu.T(N): ceil to 10 ps of ( t_zcs_rise(bank 2, MEASURED at this N) + 73.5 ps ), where 73.5 ps = the committed dV=1.65 working row's own T minus its own t_zcs (200 - 126.5). H = 4 beats, committed. If the row FAILS at that T it is re-run at 1.25x and 1.6x T and the smallest passing T is reported, with the number of escalations recorded.
SCALING LAWS -- PRE-STATED, so the measu.level_time: reported THREE ways, never composed: (i) the scheduled beat T that passes, (ii) the MEASURED first instant every gate of bank 2 is simultaneously valid, referenced to bank 2's own rail start, (iii) the functional (fcrit S3) commit margin of bank 2's gates at bank 3's delivered rail at the instant bank 3 commits.

ENERGY LEDGER -- fixed here so no term c.E_switch_conduction: MEASURED: E_out_of_tank_rise - E_into_rail_rise - E_seriesR_rise (the integrator identity, gated at 1% by A6).
ENERGY LEDGER -- fixed here so no term c.E_switch_gate_drive: reported as a BAND at every N: (lo) the MEASURED ideal-PWL floor from this study's own egt + ehi integrators; (hi) the conventional CMOS driver cost Q_gate*VGH using the committed 0.155 fC/um fit. The hi end is DERIVED, the lo end MEASURED. Neither may be omitted.
ENERGY LEDGER -- fixed here so no term c.E_timer: NOT simulated. Reported at TWO pre-stated values: 0 (an impossible free timer, so the row is a strict BOUND) and 3.5227 fJ/bank/hop (the campaign's measured ideal-PWL floor, the value at which the campaign's own admission rule gives N_min ~ 51.9). Labelled ASSUMED.
ENERGY LEDGER -- fixed here so no term c.E_bank_per_hop: E_tank_loss + E_switch_gate_drive + E_timer. The switch conduction and series R are INSIDE E_tank_loss (they are losses from the tank) and must not be added again -- stated here because double-counting them is the obvious way to get a flattering or a damning number by accident.
ENERGY LEDGER -- fixed here so no term c.E_per_gate: E_bank_per_hop / N. The denominator is the bank population, not the number of TOGGLING gates: QAL pays every beat with no activity discount, which is the committed fair-comparison convention (2*f_adia, crossover_map f4fbc9e).

PRE-STATED EXPECTATION -- my honest pred.does_per_gate_energy_fall_with_N: YES, and NOT as 1/N. I predict E_per_gate(N) = a + b/sqrt(N) + c/N with a > 0: the timer term amortises as 1/N, the switch GATE-DRIVE term as 1/sqrt(N) (because W must grow as sqrt(N)), and the switch CONDUCTION and cell/logic terms not at all per gate (constant Q means a constant fractional resonant loss; the logic work is intrinsically per gate).
PRE-STATED EXPECTATION -- my honest pred.where_per_gate_cost_stops_falling -- pre: I predict the amortisation is defeated by the SWITCH, but through its WIDTH requirement rather than through a fixed charge: the per-op switch charge is NOT fixed, it grows as sqrt(N), so the per-gate switch drive falls only as 1/sqrt(N) and the falling is over once it reaches the constant floor a. I predict the knee -- the N past which per-gate energy improves by less than 10% per doubling -- lands at N = 64 to 128. I further predict a SECOND, growing term that the brief's arithmetic does not contain and that I expect to be visible by N = 128: the fixed 10 ohm inductor series resistance is NOT scaled with the bank, so its fractional loss pi/Q_R grows as sqrt(N), and the HOLD interval grows as sqrt(N) too (T tracks t_hop at fixed H), so the leaked/drooped charge over the hold grows. If per-gate energy turns UP before N=256, that is the term I expect to be responsible, and the diagnostic is that E_seriesR/E_tank_loss and the hold droop both rise as sqrt(N) while the switch terms fall.
PRE-STATED EXPECTATION -- my honest pred.IS THERE A CROSSING -- pre-stated: AGAINST THE EASY BAR (10.0831 fJ per inverter hi+lo cycle) I predict QAL is ALREADY BELOW IT at N = 8 at dV = 1.65 (the committed row's own tank loss is 47.3 fJ for 8 gates = 5.9 fJ/gate, plus 0.9-5.4 fJ/gate of switch drive) and stays below it at every larger N -- so that bar will be crossed and crossing it MEANS NOTHING and I will say so. AGAINST THE HARD BAR (4.14 fJ per cell per op) I predict a crossing DOES exist and lands at N = 64, with per-gate energy 2.5 to 4.0 fJ at the ideal-PWL switch drive and E_timer = 0, and 3.5 to 5.5 fJ at the conventional switch driver -- i.e. I expect the crossing to be REAL at the floor and MARGINAL-to-ABSENT once the switch driver is charged conventionally. Numerically at N=64 I predict: t_zcs_rise 340-380 ps, T 420-460 ps, I_pk 3.2-3.6 mA, W 84.9 um, Q_gate 13.2 fC, E_tank_loss 250-330 fJ.
PRE-STATED EXPECTATION -- my honest pred.LEVEL TIME I expect to pay for it: at N=64 the level time is 420-460 ps against 200 ps at N=8 and the CMOS block's 92.8 ps per level (928 ps / 10 levels) -- so I predict the crossing, if it exists, is bought at 4.5-5.0x the CMOS level time, and that the honest headline is a THROUGHPUT-FOR-ENERGY trade on independent lanes, not a speed win. I pre-state that I do NOT expect this phase to produce a speed win of any kind, because nothing in a bank-width sweep can make a level faster -- widening a bank makes it slower by sqrt(N) by construction. The speed lever is Phase 2.
PRE-STATED EXPECTATION -- my honest pred.what_would_refute_my_expectation: (1) per-gate energy flat or rising from N=8 -> the fixed overhead the brief's arithmetic assumes is not fixed and the whole amortisation premise is dead; (2) A1 failing at some N -> a wide bank does not compute, and then the crossing is unreachable regardless of energy; (3) W/2 costing nothing at N=256 -> the switch scales slower than sqrt(N) and the crossing is better and earlier than I said; (4) 2W still gaining -> worse and later.

RUNTIME PLAN -- stated up front because.box: 16 cores, 31 G RAM, load ~1.1, 8.0 G free disk.
RUNTIME PLAN -- stated up front because.concurrency: <= 6 heavy Xyce jobs, and NEVER before the private PyMS vae cache is warm from a single sequential tiny deck (the committed race trap: N concurrent launches race the cache build and leave an incomplete .so.build).
RUNTIME PLAN -- stated up front because.device_count: 3 banks x N cells x 2 devices + 3 switch triples = 6N + 9 devices. N=256 -> 1545 devices.
RUNTIME PLAN -- stated up front because.disk_control: probe .prn deleted after its zero is read; row .prn kept only for the sweep rows (minimal column set) and deleted for the W and control rows after extraction. df checked before each concurrent batch and the batch is not launched below 2.0 G free.
RUNTIME PLAN -- stated up front because.escalation: if a row exceeds 3600 s it is killed, recorded as TIMEOUT, and retried once at the scaled max step doubled; if it times out again the point is reported as UNMEASURED with its wall clock, not estimated.
RUNTIME PLAN -- stated up front because.order: N ascending, so that a runtime blow-up at large N leaves a complete small-N series rather than a hole in the middle.

LABELLING DISCIPLINE: Every number in RESULTS.json carries MEASURED, DERIVED or ASSUMED. Anything modelled as an ideal source is a BOOKING and its row is a BOUND: in this deck that is (i) the +1.5 V switch gate-drive rail VHI, (ii) bank 1's N ideal DC input sources, (iii) the absent buck/converter, (iv) the absent timer. All four are named in the row. No single-hop number is ever quoted as a chain result and the tank-only energy is never quoted as the bank energy.
